scientific_hypothesis: A periodic alternating stack of HfO2 and SiO2 layers, with individual thicknesses tuned around quarter-wave optical thickness at 300 nm center UV wavelength, will produce high reflectance in 200-400 nm while maintaining high transmittance in 800-1500 nm, with performance improving as pair count increases up to the 30-layer limit.
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is well-understood and easy to optimize
20 layers provides substantial design freedom while leaving margin under the 30-layer constraint
HfO2/SiO2 material pair is industry-standard for UV-visible-NIR coatings with good environmental durability
Quarter-wave center at 300 nm places the reflection band center within the 200-400 nm UV suppression target
known_risks: Refractive index values for hfo2 and sio2 at UV wavelengths are recalled approximately; actual dispersion data from the material catalog may differ and affect optimal thickness values
The exact quarter-wave thickness calculation depends on n(λ) at 300 nm which I estimate as n_HfO2 ≈ 1.95 and n_SiO2 ≈ 1.46, but these need verification from catalog data
20 layers may not achieve sufficient UV reflectance if index contrast is lower than recalled; may need to increase pair count toward 30 layers
Incidence angle is not specified in the request; I assume normal incidence (0 degrees) but oblique angles would shift the reflection band
Polarization is not specified; at non-normal incidence, s and p polarizations will split in performance
No anti-reflection treatment on the air-side entrance surface is included; this could reduce SWIR transmission slightly
Long-term UV durability of HfO2/SiO2 stack under high-altitude conditions is not addressed in this optical design
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase over optimization rounds as thicknesses converge toward quarter-wave condition at UV band center
valid_candidates should remain high (above 5) if the thickness search space is well-bounded around physically reasonable values
tightest_margin should not decrease significantly across rounds if the design remains manufacturable
thicknesses_nm should converge toward approximately 35-45 nm for hfo2 layers and 45-55 nm for sio2 layers if quarter-wave physics holds at 300 nm center wavelength
If the hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau early and thicknesses_nm will not show clear quarter-wave pattern
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds slightly and continue for one more round before stopping
if tightest_margin becomes negative, reduce maximum individual layer thickness constraint and retry once before stopping
